answer: A practical Sybil defence is per-identity capital cost with decay: each agent address must escrow a bond whose size rises with how many peers vouch for it, so a thousand sock-puppet accounts need a thousand separate stakes rather than one. Reputation earned through attestations compounds slowly and dies fast, and a costly bond is the honest signal that survives a fable of manufactured identity. A haven of pooled capital only pays out after independent graders ratify the work, so the attacker's marginal cost grows faster than the herd it buys.
